name: Ant Burrow stage card (SS)
description:
The picture on the Ant Burrow card in Feelers' map select. The card used to photograph the real generator into a dynamic texture on every resize; this is the same burrow drawn once, and chosen rather than rolled.

A burrow is a lattice — chambers with a way out of each side and masses of earth left standing between them — and that is what the picture is: twelve hand-placed lattice corners, all but two of them off the canvas so the chambers carry on past the frame, legs of earth between them with a doorway cut through each, and two walls missing altogether, which is the other way through a burrow and the reason a chamber never reads as a box. The earth is drawn in the run's own two passes — every contour, then every fill — so no mass outlines the one beside it, and its surface is laid inside the masses from the middle out, sized to the room left where each patch lands, so nothing hangs over a contour. $carapace.dark for the earth and $ink.dark for its contour are the run's EARTH_INK and EARTH_RIM_INK to within a value or two; the floor is $dead.dark under the gouges the digging left.

It stands where the run stands. A desktop sees about 1070 world px of a 600px lattice, which is a chamber and its neighbours' walls; the first draft of this card stood three cells back and came out a floor plan — rooms small enough to read as cells in a grid rather than as places, and earth with no room on it for a surface. Two cells across the frame is the run's own distance, and it is what buys the earth its grain, the doorways their width and the fungi a size you can see them at.

Authored 3:2; the card covers its strip with this and crops off the middle, so the lattice reads at any shape the card can give it. The husks the burrow also carries are on the floor as chips instead: whole, at a size that reads on a card this small, $husk is the brightest ink in a picture whose subject is earth.
